source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 1 (Chemical Reactions and Equations).

sections.heading: 1. Chemical Reactions and Equations
points: A **chemical reaction** occurs when reactants change into new products with different properties; signs: change in **state, colour, temperature, gas evolution, or precipitate**.
A **chemical equation** represents a reaction with symbols/formulae; it must be **balanced** to obey the **Law of Conservation of Mass** (mass is neither created nor destroyed).
Balancing means equal numbers of each atom on both sides; states are shown as (s), (l), (g), (aq).

sections.heading: 2. Types of Chemical Reactions
points: **Combination** — two or more reactants form a single product (e.g. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂; burning of coal).
**Decomposition** — a single reactant breaks down (by heat = thermal, light = photolytic, electricity = electrolytic), e.g. 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃; CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
**Displacement** — a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one (Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu).
**Double displacement** — exchange of ions, often forming a **precipitate** (Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄↓ + NaCl).

sections.heading: 3. Oxidation, Reduction and Redox
points: **Oxidation** = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen (or loss of electrons); **Reduction** = loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen (gain of electrons).
A **redox reaction** = oxidation and reduction occur together (e.g. CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O: CuO reduced, H₂ oxidised).
**Exothermic** reactions release heat (respiration, combustion); **endothermic** absorb heat.

sections.heading: 4. Corrosion and Rancidity
points: **Corrosion** — metals are attacked by moisture/air/acids; iron forms **rust (hydrated iron oxide)**; silver blackens, copper turns green.
Prevention: painting, oiling, greasing, **galvanisation (zinc coating)**, electroplating, alloying.
**Rancidity** — oils/fats get oxidised, giving bad smell/taste; prevented by **antioxidants**, airtight containers, refrigeration, flushing with **nitrogen** (as in chip packets).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Balanced equation ↔ Law of Conservation of Mass.
Reaction types: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement.
Oxidation = gain of oxygen/loss of hydrogen; Reduction = opposite; both together = redox.
Rust = hydrated iron(III) oxide; galvanisation = zinc coating.
Rancidity prevented by antioxidants + nitrogen flushing.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Balancing** equations follows the **Law of Conservation of Mass**.
**Galvanisation** = coating iron with **zinc** (not tin).
**Respiration is exothermic** (releases energy); **decomposition** is often endothermic.
Chip packets are flushed with **nitrogen** to prevent **rancidity** (oxidation).
